title: how a file that hangs the parser is skipped instead of hanging the build
summary: One pathological file can no longer hang a build: every parse path (keeper full build, the reader's in-process fallback, and the incremental patch) goes through parseFile, which runs the file's whole synchronous parse as ONE vm call with a 5s timeout, so a spin in JS, regex or tree-sitter wasm is cut off even though the event loop is dead. The file is then indexed by path only (timedOut), reported to the log and repair.jsonl as parse-timeout (which status shows as the last failure), its fingerprint is stamped so restarts do not re-parse it, and fresh tree-sitter parsers are swapped in. Before this, the same file made every find wait 180s for nothing, kept the keeper at 100% CPU forever, and a reader falling back to an in-process build hung with no limit.

steps.role: does the async work (grammar load, read, Rust workspace lookup) first, then runs parseByLanguage + extractContentTokens under runWithTimeout; on timeout resets parsers and returns a path-only result
the vm trampoline whose watchdog thread stops a synchronous spin
replaces every loaded parser; a parser stopped mid-parse otherwise fails all later files
full build: reports a timedOut parse and keeps the file
incremental patch: same report, the edited hanging file is retried and cut off again
parse-timeout event in repair.jsonl, surfaced by status

invariants: No await may sit inside the guarded section — only synchronous work is stoppable, so I/O (like findRustWorkspace) runs before it.
resetParsers must run after every timeout: with it disabled, tests/parse-timeout.test.ts sees RuntimeError: Aborted() on every later file of that grammar.
Does not stop a hang inside Node native code (sync fs on a dead mount); inflight.json still names those.
